text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- GOVT DECIDES TODAY ON INTEREST RATES
The Central Bank's Monetary Policy Committee meets today to set the Basic Interest Rate of the Central Bank (TBC) and the so-called Tban rate for October.

Finance Ministry and Central Bank officials are convinced that there are internal and external limits to a reduction in interest rates, despite pressure from some economic sectors for a rate cut following lower inflation in August and September.
-- PARANA WANTS TO EXPORT WHEAT
Wheat producers in Brazil's southern state of Parana are studying the possibility of exporting wheat to Venezuela, South Africa, China and Egypt.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- 47 PCT ERR USING ELECTRONIC VOTE METHOD

Ten days ahead of the municipal elections, nearly half of Sao Paulo voters which has already chosen a candidate do not know how to use the electronic vote system. A Datafolha poll interviewed 1,731 voters, of which 93 percent already have a candidate.
-- GANGS OF TEENAGERS USE REVOLVERS
Gangs of teenagers are using guns all over the country. Stray bullets shot during gang fights have caused the death of two girls in the last 35 days.
O GLOBO
-- MILITARY POLICE'S SECRET SERVICE WILL SUPERVISE ELECTION IN RIO
Fifty military policemen will supervise the first round of the municipal elections on October 3 in Rio de Janeiro city.
-- PAES WILL APPEAL TO COURT IF PMDB BACKS REELECTION
After President Fernando Henrique Cardoso admitted he might be candidate for reelection in 1998, opposing parties have rushed to avoid the approval of the reelection proposal.

Deputy Paes de Andrade, president of the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB), threatened to appeal to court if the party nominates members for the special panel which will discuss the reelection amendment in the lower house.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo newsroom, 55-11-2324411
